_note: World Series operations launcher (ws_operate.py). Every number here is PROVISIONAL unless its note says measured. Paths: '~' is expanded; relative paths are relative to code_dir. Changing a value between games is fine; the supervisor reads this file once when it starts.
ops_root_note: Outside the repository. Holds status.json (the alert watcher's contract), supervisor.lock and runs/<KST date>/. Env PITCHEEZY_WS_OPS_ROOT overrides.
code_dir_note: The checkout whose publisher runs. null = the checkout that contains this file. Its HEAD (clean, tracked files) is recorded at the first start of a date; a restart or a new start onto a different commit is refused while a game of that date is not final (deploy only between games).
expect_commit_note: Optional full sha: start refuses if code_dir HEAD differs (pin the launch candidate). --expect-commit overrides.
publish_config_note: Copied per run to runs/<date>/publish_config.runtime.json (mode 0600) with fixed_delay_s and upload filled in by the launcher. The repository file is never edited.
game_types_note: statsapi gameType values the launcher operates. W = World Series.
fixed_delay_note: The one delay every viewer gets (publish_config fixed_delay_s). 15 s by Song decision 2026-10-19 (BLK-03; revisit after WS Game 1 with measured upload/CDN delay). Must not exceed the live feed's max_delay_s (120): the publisher refuses to start otherwise.
lead_note: The publisher starts this long before the earliest scheduled first pitch of the date (the rehearsal used 15; 30 leaves room for one restart before first pitch and for the pre-game game file).
settle_note: Stop this long after every operated game of the date is final in the published game file (late scoring corrections are still published while running).
hard_end_note: Stop at the latest scheduled start + this, whatever the game state (9 h: a long extra-inning game plus a rain delay). The childwatch deadline is this + childwatch_slack_s.
armb_note: auto = recommendation (ARM-B, MPS) on only if available memory at start >= armb_min_available_bytes (8 GiB, as the rehearsal). '0' / '1' force it; '1' below the floor is refused.
profile_sources_note: null = take PITCHEEZY_OBSERVER_PROFILE_SOURCES from the launching shell (the daily LATEST.json pointer). A missing value is a warning, not a refusal (the reference card is then absent).
player_snapshot_dir_note: Pre-game season stats cache (<game_pk>.json per game; OPS-06). null = take PITCHEEZY_PLAYER_SNAPSHOT_DIR from the launching shell. Must be an existing directory outside any git checkout. Unset: the publisher gets no such variable and pregame is null (unchanged). Set but missing, not a directory or inside a checkout: a warning, not a refusal, and the variable is not forwarded (pregame null). Replace cache files and restart the publisher only between games.

restart.note: Unexpected publisher exit (or a hung publisher: health.json has not advanced for health_stall_s, counted from the later of segment start and the last new sequence, so the first stall restart is at least 300 s after a segment start; startup_grace_s only delays when the check begins) -> restart after backoff_s[i] (last value repeats), at most max_restarts times per supervisor run (a new start of the same date after an operator stop begins again at 0). 3 restarts cover a transient crash or two without turning a deterministic crash into a loop that re-polls MLB and re-warms ARM-B every few seconds; the waits (30/60/120 s) let the output lock and the upload child go away and give the alert watcher time to see the outage (worst case 3.5 min of planned waiting).

start_confirm_note: After spawning the detached supervisor, start waits this long for its supervisor_start event (OPS-02 drill: a supervisor that died at once used to go unnoticed). Not seen and the process is gone -> start writes state refused with urgent start_refused (problem key supervisor_not_started in the message) and exits 2; still running -> a warning only (it owns status.json once it takes the lock).
start_retry_note: The start command itself (e.g. the 07:00 launchd job) retries transient problems (schedule request failed, disk, T7, another publisher, other unfinished games) every start_retry_s for up to start_retry_window_s, never past the publisher start time. A refusal for any reason is written to status.json (state refused, urgent problem start_refused) unless a supervisor holds the lock; --dry-run never retries or writes.
prestart_note: Checks at publisher start. Transient problems (schedule request failed with no recorded game list, memory/disk below the start floor, T7 not mounted, another publisher still running, other unfinished games) are retried every prestart_retry_s until first pitch (started after first pitch: for prestart_late_window_s), then the date ends refused with an urgent problem. A failed schedule request falls back to the game list recorded at start (RUN.json). Any other problem refuses at once.

guards.note: stop_* end the publisher for the date (the machine and the recorder come first); warn_* and health_stale_warn_s only raise an alert in status.json. Memory = vm_stat free+inactive+speculative (the measure of the 10/12-13 trials).

upload.note: Upload stays off unless this is true AND start is given --upload AND the credentials are present in the environment (token: PITCHEEZY_PUBLISH_TOKEN or a token file path in PITCHEEZY_WS_OPS_TOKEN_FILE; host: PITCHEEZY_WS_OPS_UPLOAD_BASE_URL). Values are never printed or logged, only their presence.
